proof:
# Exact simplex cap moments and a balanced density conservation law

Let Delta_d={xi in R^(d+1): xi_j>=0, sum xi_j=1}, d>=1, with uniform probability measure mu. Coordinates and centroids below are barycentric; their sum is one. Let

    H={xi:c dot xi>=0}

be a proper cap, meaning its cutting plane meets the relative interior of Delta_d. Write P=mu(H), and let b be the centroid of the actual (d-1)-dimensional section. For d=1 this centroid is the unique section point. Let L>0 be the normalized coarea of the section: equivalently L is the derivative at zero of mu{c dot xi>=-s} in s. Define its unnormalized cap first moments M_j=int_H xi_j dmu.

Then the exact identity is

    M_j=[P+L c_j b_j]/(d+1),   j=0,...,d.           (1)

This holds with repeated raw coefficients, zero raw coefficients, and section incidences through vertices or faces, provided the section is proper. No section is replaced by an average or a cap centroid.

## 1. Elementary divergence proof

In the affine simplex use the tangent vector field

    V_j(xi)=xi_j(e_j-xi).

Its divergence, taken in the d-dimensional affine space with constant volume measure, is 1-(d+1)xi_j. To check this directly in coordinates xi_1,...,xi_d, first take j>0. The j-coordinate derivative is 1-2xi_j, and the other d-1 diagonal derivatives are -xi_j. For j=0 use xi_0=1-sum_(k>0)xi_k; the coordinate field is -xi_0 xi_k, whose diagonal derivatives sum to 1-(d+1)xi_0.

The normal flux of V_j vanishes on every original facet of the simplex: on xi_j=0 the vector field vanishes, and on any other facet it is tangent. On the interior cutting plane, c dot xi=0, so the normal numerator is

    c dot V_j=xi_j c_j.

The outward normal of the captured set points toward c dot xi<0. Integrating divergence over the cut simplex, and dividing by its original volume, therefore gives

    P-(d+1)M_j=-L c_j b_j.

This is (1). The divergence theorem applies to this bounded polytope even when the plane passes through an original face; such incidences merely merge or remove boundary pieces of lower surface measure. In d=1 it is the same fundamental-theorem-of-calculus calculation on an interval.

The identity automatically sums correctly: sum_j M_j=P, because sum b_j c_j=0, the equation of the actual section centroid.

## 2. Exponential normalization

Let E_0,...,E_d be independent unit-rate exponentials and put V=sum_j c_j E_j. Write f=f_V(0). Then

    L=d f.                                         (2)

Indeed G=sum E_j has Gamma(d+1,1) law, Xi=E/G is uniform on Delta_d, and G,Xi are independent. If U=c dot Xi, its density at zero is L. Conditioning on G gives f_V(0)=L E(G^(-1))=L/d. The integral E(G^(-1))=Gamma(d)/Gamma(d+1)=1/d is finite for every d>=1. A proper section has both positive and negative raw coefficients, so its density is continuous at zero; the conditioning identity also follows by integrating the section coarea near zero and applying dominated convergence. Formula (2) remains valid when some coefficients vanish.

Thus (1) is equivalently

    int_H xi_j dmu=[P+d f c_j b_j]/(d+1).           (3)

The factor d is essential.

## 3. A joint mass and barycenter identity

Take finitely many proper caps H_i with raw normals c_i, cap probabilities P_i, positive exponential densities f_i, and the SAME actual section centroid b. Suppose

    sum_i c_i=0.

Define T=sum_i P_i/f_i>0 and the nonnegative density

    w(xi)=sum_i 1_(H_i)(xi)/f_i.

Then

    int w dmu=T,
    int xi_j w dmu=T/(d+1) for every j.              (4)

The first identity is its definition. For the second, sum (3)/f_i and use the actual raw-normal balance. Consequently w/T is a probability density with exactly the ordinary simplex centroid. The density is determined by the real caps; it is neither a formal allocation of independent cap masses nor a distribution replacing the original uniform measure in a geometric conclusion.

More generally, positive coefficients alpha_i with sum alpha_i c_i=0 give the same result for w=sum alpha_i 1_Hi/f_i and T=sum alpha_i P_i/f_i. This is just (4) applied to the positively rescaled normals alpha_i c_i; their exponential densities are f_i/alpha_i.

## 4. The full-row capacity normalization

For a nonnegative row x let

    phi_d(x)=inf_(t>0) t / Pr(x dot Xi<=t)^(1/d),

where thresholds of zero captured probability are excluded. Consider a finite family of positive rows x_i summing componentwise to 1, with proper differentiable minimizing thresholds t_i and common actual section centroid b. Put

    c_i=t_i 1-x_i,
    P_i=Pr(c_i dot Xi>=0).

At a proper interior minimizing threshold, differentiation gives t_i L_i=d P_i. By (2),

    t_i=P_i/f_i.                                   (5)

Every cut passes through its centroid, so t_i=b dot x_i. Summing the rows gives sum t_i=1 and hence sum c_i=0. Equations (4)--(5) now give the exact normalization

    int sum_i 1_Hi/f_i dmu=1,
    int xi_j sum_i 1_Hi/f_i dmu=1/(d+1).            (6)

Thus an actual stationary full-row family supplies a barycenter-preserving probability reweighting of uniform simplex measure, with the explicit indicator density in (6).

It is not asserted that every barycenter-preserving density arises from such a family, that (6) alone controls the probabilities P_i, or that the reweighted measure is uniform. In particular any proposed stochastic-matrix or convex-order consequence must use more than just the displayed total mass unless that implication is independently proved.
